elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Contractor must “defend ... Company and its affiliates against any third-party claim” arising from the enumerated matters.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Contractor must “indemnify Company and its affiliates against any third-party claim” arising from the enumerated matters.

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Clause (d)(i) covers allegations that the “Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Clause (d)(ii) expressly covers “Contractor's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Clause (d)(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company data caused by Contractor, an operative formulation of a Contractor-caused data breach.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Clause (d)(iv) expressly covers “Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.”

elements.element: Customer must provide prompt notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Company must give Contractor “prompt written notice of the claim.”

elements.element: Vendor must be permitted to control the defense of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Company must “allow Contractor to control the defense of the claim.”

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation regarding the defense.
Any Customer indemnity must be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Neither the original nor rendered language imposes any indemnity obligation on Company. Because the conditional Customer-indemnity obligation is demonstrably absent, Company has no indemnity exposure beyond—or even within—the two permitted grounds.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Clause (d)(i) requires Contractor to indemnify Company against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion addresses modifications made by or for Company.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
The IP-infringement remedies must permit Vendor to procure continued usage rights.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no obligation or option to procure continued usage rights.

elements.element: The IP-infringement remedies must permit Vendor to modify the affected services or deliverables to become non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The IP-infringement remedies must permit Vendor to replace the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing alternatives.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The IP-infringement remedies must provide a refund if the other remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to 3× annual fees.
elements.evidence: No liability cap or 3× annual-fees super-cap applies to the indemnity.

result.reason: The added clause fully implements the preferred Vendor indemnity, including all required triggers and the specified notice, control, and cooperation procedures. No Customer indemnity is imposed, so the limitation on any such indemnity is satisfied. The fallback is not satisfied because all specified IP exclusions, infringement remedies, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are omitted. The insertion is confined to the requested indemnity and leaves the existing attorney-fee language unchanged; that language can operate as a fee-shifting rule for suits between the parties without negating Contractor's duty to provide a third-party defense.
